text:
Predicates:
GoodGuy(x) ::: x is a good guy.
Wins(x) ::: x wins.
SuperheroMovie(x) ::: x is a superhero movie.
Fights(x, y) ::: x fights y.
NamedAfter(x, y) ::: x is named after y.
AppearsIn(x, y) ::: x appears in y.
Premises:
∀x (SuperheroMovie(x) → ∀y (GoodGuy(y) → Wins(y))) ::: In superhero movies, the good guys always win.
SuperheroMovie(surprisingAdventures) ::: The Surprising Adventures of Sir Digby Chicken Caesar is a superhero movie.
∀x ∀y (Fights(x, y) ↔ (GoodGuy(x) ∧ ¬GoodGuy(y))) ::: Good guys fight bad guys and vice versa.
Fights(sirDigby, nemesis) ::: Sir Digby fights his nemesis.
∀x ∀y (SuperheroMovie(x) ∧ NamedAfter(x, y) → GoodGuy(y)) ::: If a superhero movie is named after a character, that character is a good guy.
NamedAfter(surprisingAdventures, sirDigby) ::: The Surprising Adventures of Sir Digby Chicken Caesar is named after Sir Digby.
∀x ∀y (Wins(x) ∧ Fights(x, y) → ¬Wins(y)) ::: If somebody wins a fight, the person they are fighting loses.
∀x ∀y (SuperheroMovie(x) ∧ NamedAfter(x, y) → AppearsIn(y, x)) ::: If a superhero movie is named after a character, that character appears in the movie.
Conclusion:
¬Wins(nemesis) ::: Sir Digby’s nemesis loses.
